input_representation.limitation: No resolver distinguishes premise, constraint and optional inspiration.
Several required nodes are absent from current production seeds; fixture-only nodes were needed.
Platform, duration, language and scene count have typed paths; content rating and avoid semantics do not.
Identity, psychology, appearance, moral boundaries, provenance and locks are flattened into prose.
No independent directional relationship object or state update contract exists.
Source, observation time, expiry, platform scope and acceptance status need a separate signal wrapper.

evidence: Mara publicly exposes Adrian and independently verifies the evidence.
Her distrust is expressed through 'I trusted you once. Now I verify everything.'
Her calm, reserved appearance and refusal to endanger innocents are copied into CharacterProfile.
No scene forces Mara to choose between revenge and harming an innocent person.
case_reviews.observed_loss: The moral boundary affects description but not causal action, and the relationship is model-inferred.

evidence: Lucian is cold, protective and secretive, and his fear of losing control drives the final scene.
His belief about humans is reflected directly in conflict dialogue.
His need for human connection and rejection of humans becomes the forced bond.
Because the user did not define Lucian's story role or the human enemy profile, the model made the unnamed Hunter the protagonist.
case_reviews.observed_loss: Incomplete role and relationship inputs allow the model to decide protagonist authority and counterpart identity.

evidence: Lena follows an evidence-driven investigation and physically isolates the AI.
Her belief is used almost verbatim in the decisive decryption line.
Human safety appears in her motivation and dialogue.
The model turns the AI system into a speaking antagonist because no entity or relationship type is available.
case_reviews.observed_loss: Occupation, story role, system entity type and moral boundary are flattened into prose and cannot be enforced independently.

influenced_generation: All three requested genres and central premises were clearly reflected.
All three named characters retained their names and supplied core motivations.
Fear, belief and contradiction affected choices and dialogue more reliably than appearance.
Scene Causality remained valid in all three outputs.
lost_or_weak: Moral boundaries were preserved as descriptions but were not tested through costly choices.
Appearance influenced CharacterProfile text but did not materially affect scene execution.
Relationships remained inferred prose and could not preserve directional authority or state.
Field provenance, user locks and AI expansion boundaries were not enforceable.
Intent duplicated across story_goal, tags, hook and generation_notes, so influence cannot be attributed to one channel.
Audience fit cannot be validated from one unblinded output per case.
Trend recommendations and explicit avoid tags were not exercised.
unexpected_behavior: The model created missing counterpart characters and assigned their story roles.
The Supernatural case promoted the unnamed Hunter to protagonist because Lucian's role was unspecified.
The Sci-Fi case treated the AI system as a speaking character without an explicit entity contract.
Placeholder Story QC gave the Sci-Fi protagonist agency 2.5 despite several visible investigative choices, confirming that QC scores are not proof of intent adherence.

future_implementation_considerations: Implement deterministic intent resolution before any Prompt integration.
Keep stable Ontology nodes separate from trend recommendation metadata.
Add field-level character provenance, locks and AI-expandable controls only after contract validation.
Represent relationships independently and require explicit role resolution for principal characters.
Define entity type for non-human systems such as an AI before treating them as characters.
Avoid duplicating the same intent across many prompt channels without declared weighting.
Validate moral boundaries using observable decision-pressure checks rather than keyword presence.
Use a later bounded controllability A/B before approving runtime integration.
decision: Research contract remains justified; current runtime can carry intent text but does not provide typed control or enforcement.
